description.value: A longitudinal fMRI study examined emotion regulation-related BOLD responses before and after cognitive behavioral therapy in participants with major depressive disorder and healthy controls.

spans.text: We used a modified version of this task to examine the neural correlates of voluntary emotion regulation in a group of individuals with current MDD, both before and after a course of CBT for depression.

definition.value: Change in emotion regulation-dependent reduction of BOLD signal from time 1 to time 2 for MDD participants was correlated with treatment outcome (defined as final BDI score while controlling for time 1 BDI);

spans.text: Change in emotion regulation-dependent reduction of BOLD signal from time 1 to time 2 for MDD participants was correlated with treatment outcome (defined as final BDI score while controlling for time 1 BDI), in a whole-brain analysis at a priori statistical threshhold (voxel-wise z > 3.1, cluster-wise FWE-corrected p < 0.05) in medial frontal pole, left subgenual cingulate, lingual gyrus/cerebellum, left precentral/supramarginal gyrus, and left putamen (4 clusters, Figure 4 and Table 3 ).

value: Greater emotion regulation-dependent reduction of BOLD signal in these clusters at time 2 than at time 1 was associated with better treatment outcome.
The primary finding of this study is that emotion regulation-dependent reduction in BOLD signal is enhanced longitudinally as a function of clinical improvement with CBT for depression.
